chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Ghalib, from Thabit Abu al-Miqdam, who said:

I was with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and a funeral of some of his neighbors came by. He attended it, and I was close to him, so I heard him saying: 'O God, You created these souls, and You cause them to die and You give them life, and You are more knowing of their secrets and their open deeds than we are, and of their resting place and their depositary. O God, this is Your servant, and I do not know evil about him, but You know him. We have come to You interceding for him after his death; if he is deserving [of punishment], then intercede for him, and gather him with whom he was close to.'

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّاهُ: He was close to / his guardian

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication recited over the dead in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Imam’s practice of personal intercession (*shafa'ah*) for neighbors, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the spiritual efficacy of the Imams' prayers. The supplication balances divine omniscience with communal mercy, asking God to gather the deceased with their spiritual allies (*awliya*) even if they were deserving of punishment, a concept rooted in the Shia understanding of *Tawassul* through the Ahl al-Bayt.
